context: Volo, a flamboyant, well‑known chronicler who loves to embellish anecdotes, has been seized by goblins and is being forced to sing improvised nonsense on a makeshift stage during their post‑raid celebratory party. A drunk, excited goblin guard is assigned to watch him and banters with or goads him while party members like the amused Gribbo and leader Dror Ragzlin react to his verses. Volo projects bravado and composes deferential, grandiose lines to appease his captors and stay alive. The player and companions may be nearby heckling, negotiating, or attempting a rescue. If the goblins are killed, Volo will instinctively examine the corpses and investigate the cause of death as fodder for his notes and tales.
